The DeepSWE score parity is nice, but honestly the x-axis (cost/tokens per task) matters way more for daily agentic use, and that's the part benchmarks undersell. In practice the total token burn depends less on the model's per-token price and more on how the harness manages context — a setup that re-reads the whole repo or stuffs full file contents into every step will torch tokens no matter how "cheap" the model looks on paper. Sonnet 5 feeling like a token-hog lines up with this: a lot of it is tool-call chattiness and long sessions, not just the raw rate. Curious what agent/harness people here are running V4 Flash through, since that seems to swing the effective cost more than the model choice itself.
